title: The cohomology projection onto the inverse limit is epi

from.place: proof, the corresponding kernel/cokernel half of the five-term sequence

statement: Let $i\in\mathbf Z$, let $K:\mathbf N^{op}\to D(\mathrm{Ab})$ [def-weil-inverse-system, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] have a product, and let $(L,p,\delta)$ be a specified distinguished Roos triangle [def-weil-derived-limit]. If $b:H^i(L)\to\lim H^i(K)$ is any map satisfying $b\,\pi_n=H^i(p\,\mathrm{pr}_n)$ for every $n\in\mathbf N$, then $b$ is an epimorphism of abelian groups [def-sp-abelian]. The inverse limit is the categorical limit, not a separately chosen kernel object.

source.place: Tag 07KY, kernel half of the long exact sequence; derived.tex Tag 07KC

proof.text: Use exact products of abelian groups and the existing derived-product theorem to obtain preservation of countable products by H^i, with projection-compatible comparison isomorphism.

For an element y of the inverse limit, pull its coordinate tuple back through the comparison. The limit cone equations and the defining formula for 1-s show that this element x lies in the kernel of H^i(1-s). Joint injectivity of the mapped product projections proves the zero equation.

Exactness of the long cohomology sequence supplies z with H^i(p)(z)=x. The projection equations for b imply that b(z) and y have the same limit coordinates, hence are equal. Thus b is surjective, equivalent to epi in abelian groups. This proof is implemented in Lean, using ab_exact_iff and Concrete.limit_ext.
